newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: M&S opens Prague store, eyes Poland.
newsitem.headline: M&S opens Prague store, eyes Poland.

text.p: British-based retailer Marks & Spencer Plc on Tuesday opened its first store in the Czech Republic, a 1,500 square-metre outlet in Prague's new Myslbek shopping centre in the banking district.

Company officials said the firm planned to open several more stores in the country with its Czech franchisee, COMS a.s., in the near future if the Prague outlet is successful, and was looking at other countries in the region.
Marks & Spencer's Eastern Europe commercial controller Simon Innes told Reuters that Poland was the next country in the company's scope.

"We are looking at Poland at the moment, and I am sure we will look at other countries around this area. At the moment we are moving one country at the time," Innes said. "We will look at Romania, Slovakia and Estonia."
He added that the franchise scenario would likely be repeated in Poland.
"Partners bring the precious local knowledge, the expertise, the access to the market, and also the language... That way, it's a good team effort."

Chairman Dusan Mrozek of the Czech partner, COMS a.s., said that opening more stores in the country was mainly a question of finding suitable retail space in the main centres, including the cities of Brno, Ostrava and Plzen.
Mrozek said that average prices in the Prague outlet would be actually higher than in M&S stores in Britain because of transport costs, duties, and taxes.
